text:
violet: Ran into a weird logging/redaction interaction in the python onboarding sample. The request id is present for the first info line then later logs show an empty token or `-`. Repro & notes below.

omar: can you paste the snippet + env?

violet: minimal snippet:
```
2026-11-11T08:45:10Z INFO ingress request_id=hdr-42 route=/v1/complete
2026-11-11T08:45:10Z INFO model request_id= - tokens=56
2026-11-11T08:45:10Z INFO resp request_id= - status=200
```

violet: env: REDWOOD_PY=0.9.4, OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext, REDWOOD_REDACT_HEADERS="authorization,request-id", REDWOOD_LOG_REDACT=true

priya: That's very similar to other reports but this looks like a middleware ordering issue. Do we set the logger context from a copy of headers or the original header dict?

violet: logger middleware sets a contextvar early by reading request.headers.get('x-request-id') or fallback to header 'request-id'. But the redaction hook seems to canonicalize header names and then replace values in the same dict. If logger adapter reads from the original header object lazily, it will see the redacted value.

omar: I suspect two things: (1) our REDACT_HEADERS parser normalizes by stripping 'x-' which inadvertently matches both 'x-request-id' and 'request-id'; (2) our redactor mutates in place. Fix should: normalize names case-insensitively, but redact only the header keys the customer intended, and operate on a copied headers mapping.

priya: also confirm the logger context uses the value captured at request entry (preferred), not a pointer to headers. If we capture early we avoid later mutations.

violet: workaround: set REDWOOD_LOG_REDACT=false or change REDWOOD_REDACT_HEADERS to include the explicit x- prefix: "x-request-id". That preserved my logs. Not ideal for customers.

omar: I'll open INF-3421 and add a unit/integration test that asserts request_id persists across multiple log lines with redaction on.

ops-bot: INF-3421 created by omar 1: https://redwood.company/infra/INF-3421

omar: Proposed fix in words: when building sanitized headers, do header_map = dict(request.headers) then mutate header_map, attach as request.sanitized_headers. Ensure logger middleware reads request_id from original request at ingress and writes to contextvar. Add test where logger adapter queries headers after redaction to ensure no in-place mutation.

priya: add a note: we must not accidentally redact otel propagation headers (traceparent, b3) unless explicitly configured. Some customers expect those untouched. Add regression test across OTEL_PROPAGATORS permutations.

violet: thanks, will attach my failing sample to the ticket. Also adding a short FAQ blurb to onboarding README about redaction config edge cases (how to explicitly match x- prefixed headers).

omar: cool. tagging @priya for review when I open the PR. target micropatch release 0.9.5 if CI green.

ops-bot: RDW-RELEASE-948 created for INF-3421

priya: ack, will review PR quickly. :thumbsup:

violet: appreciated!
